Subject: Introduction of Credit Risk-o-Meter as an additional disclosure mechanism for debt securities

sources.label: 1791436170839 · Disclosure of 'Credit Risk-o-Meter' in respect of Debt Securities · p. 4
sources.text:
Applicability: The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all listed and proposed to be listed issuances of Non-Convertible Securities (NCS), Commercial Papers (CPs), Securitised Debt Instruments (SDIs), Security Receipts (SRs), and Structured Debt / Market Linked Debentures (MLDs), whether issued by way of public issue or private placement.

Framework for disclosure of Credit Risk-o-Meter

Credit Risk-o-Meter shall be disclosed in:

Offer document

Abridged Prospectus

Private Placement Memorandum

All advertisements of Issuer/OBPPs

Web and mobile platforms of OBPPs

Issuers/OBPPs shall display the credit risk of debt security in pictorial meter named "Credit risk-o-meter " and this meter shall appropriately depict the level of credit risk in any specific debt security.

Issuers/OBPPs shall clearly indicate that it represents only the credit risk associated with the debt security.

The Credit Risk-o-meter shall map SEBI's existing credit rating standardization framework, rating symbols (AAA to D) to following six levels of risk with corresponding colour codes in following manner:

sources.label: 1791436170839 · Subject: Introduction of Credit Risk-o-Meter as an additional disclosure mechanism for debt securities · p. 1
sources.text:
To assist investors in assessing credit risk through colour-coded visualization prior to investing, it has been decided to introduce a 'Credit Risk-o-Meter' as a mandatory component of the following:

Offer document

Abridged Prospectus

Private Placement Memorandum

All advertisements of Issuer/OBPPs

Web and mobile platforms of OBPPs

The detailed framework for disclosure of Credit Risk-o-Meter is enclosed at Annexure-A.

To give effect to the above,

(a) A new Chapter II-C, titled "Disclosure of Credit Risk-o-Meter for debt securities" shall be inserted in the Master Circular for issue and listing of Non-Convertible Securities, Securitised Debt Instruments, Security Receipts, Municipal Debt Securities and Commercial Paper ("NCS Master Circular") dated October 15, 2025.

sources.label: 1791436170839 · 2.11. Disclaimers: · p. 7
sources.text:
"The Credit risk-o-meter is based on evaluation of the credit risk of the issuer and does not constitute investment advice or a recommendation to invest. Investments in debt securities are also subject to market and liquidity risks."

In case of unsecured perpetual bonds (such as AT1 bonds), the Issuers/OBPPs shall incorporate the following disclaimer in Offer document, Abridged Prospectus and Private Placement Memorandum below the credit risk-o-meter, and display the same suitably on their web and mobile platform:

"The Credit Risk-o-Meter is based on evaluation of the credit risk of the issuer and does not reflect the unique structural risks associated with Unsecured Perpetual Bonds (such as AT1 Bonds). These instruments may carry the risk of total loss of invested capital. Investors are advised to read the Information Memorandum/Private placement Memorandum carefully before investing."

Additional requirements for OBPPs:

Any change in credit risk-o-meter of the debt security shall be communicated by OBPP on their platform, within 24 hours of receiving intimation of rating change from NSDL/CDSL.

OBPPs shall display the Credit risk-o-meter on the Bond Listing & Bond details page where all other details are prominently displayed before investment action buttons.

OBPPs shall ensure that the credit risk-o-meter is displayed or printed in all forms of advertisements that explicitly reference the rating of the debt security, irrespective of the medium or format of such advertisements.

In case of advertisements published in monochrome format, a QR code shall be provided along with credit risk-o-meter to enable investors to access the website of OBPP/Issuer and view the Credit Risk-o-Meter in the prescribed colour-coded format.

answer: AIFs can proceed with the launch of their new regular scheme after 10 working days of filing the application with SEBI, unless otherwise advised [S1].

sources.label: 1785412195539 · 2.4. Modalities for filing of PPM and launch of Regular schemes: · p. 1
sources.text:
In terms of Regulation 12 of the AIF Regulations, AIFs may launch scheme(s) subject to filing of PPM with SEBI through a SEBI registered Merchant Banker. In this context, the following is specified with respect to Regular schemes:

AIFs can proceed with launch of their new scheme after 10 working days of filing of application with SEBI, unless otherwise advised. However, AIFs can proceed with launch of their first schemes from the date of grant of SEBI registration (or) after 10 working days of filing of application with SEBI, whichever is later.

PPM of Regular schemes shall be filed, at the time of registration or prior to launch of new scheme, on SEBI Intermediary portal along with the following documents in addition to payment of applicable (scheme) fee:

sources.text:
AI only funds and LVFs:

In terms of proviso to Regulation 12(3A) of AIF Regulations, AI only funds and LVFs are exempt from filing their PPM with SEBI through Merchant Banker and incorporating comments of SEBI in their PPM i.e. AI only funds and LVFs can launch their scheme immediately upon filing of PPM with SEBI. sources.label: 1785412195539 · 2.4. Modalities for filing of PPM and launch of Regular schemes: · p. 3
sources.text:

answer: If a client squares off the sale position in securities for which they availed early pay-in (EPI) benefit, the value of EPI is removed, and any resulting margin shortfall at the client level is blocked from the proprietary collateral of the Trading Member or Clearing Member by the Clearing Corporation [S1].

citations.section: Subject: Margin Waiver on Subsequent Buy/Sell Transactions Post Early Pay-In (EPI) in Cash Segment

sources.label: 1792668596460 · Subject: Margin Waiver on Subsequent Buy/Sell Transactions Post Early Pay-In (EPI) in Cash Segment · p. 2
sources.text:
Upon the client taking position basis the EPI on same trade date in cash segment, CC shall check the availability of client margin after reducing the available value of EPI.

If client squares off the sale position in securities for which client has availed EPI benefit, the value of EPI shall be removed and any shortfall in margins at client level due to such removal of EPI value, shall be blocked from the proprietary collateral of TM/CM by the CC. This condition will not be applicable to Trade for trade (TFT) securities as such transactions are settled on gross basis.

Additionally, TMs shall be directed to ensure that their risk management allows the client to square off the position for which client has given EPI or take any new position, only if the requisite margins of the client are available with the TM.

Further, CCs are directed to:

Make amendments to the relevant bye-laws, rules and regulations for the implementation of the above framework, as may be applicable/necessary;

Carry out system changes, if any, to implement the above framework;

Disseminate the provisions of this circular on their website;

The provisions of this circular shall come into force with effect from four months from the date of issuance of this circular.

This circular is being issued in exercise of powers conferred under Section 11(1) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 read with Regulation 51 of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) (Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations) Regulations, 2018 to protect the interest of investors in securities and to promote development of, and to regulate securities market.

This circular is available on SEBI website at www.sebi.gov.in at "Legal Framework - Circulars."

The circular has been issued with the approval of the competent authority.

Yours faithfully,

sources.label: 1792668596460 · Subject: Margin Waiver on Subsequent Buy/Sell Transactions Post Early Pay-In (EPI) in Cash Segment · p. 1
sources.text:
Exchanges/Clearing Corporations (CCs) in consultation with SEBI, have issued various circulars/ guidelines on Margin collection and Reporting for the cases where the client has completed Early Pay-in of securities.

The said circulars/ guidelines inter-alia stipulate that in respect of sale of shares by a client for which EPI request via Block mechanism has been accepted, the same may be considered as margin collected towards peak margin for the said sale transaction. Further, in respect of sale of shares by a client for which EPI request via Block mechanism has been accepted and credit entry is posted of the sale value of the shares in the ledger account of the client, EPI value may be considered as margin collected towards subsequent margin requirement of the client. The sale value up to 100% of such securities (EPI value) shall be available as Margin for other positions across all the segments.

In this context, taking into account the proposals received from the Broker ISF, recommendations of Risk Management Review Committee (RMRC) of SEBI and internal deliberations, it is decided that where a client has a net sell obligation in a settlement; and the EPI request for the sold securities has been successfully accepted by the CC, the CC shall, on a real-time basis, not collect margin from the Trading Member (TM)/ Clearing Member (CM) on the subsequent buy/sell positions of the client, up to the amount of such accepted EPI.

The aforesaid facility shall be implemented in the following manner:

Upon EPI accepted, CC on trade date shall compute the available value of EPI which shall be lower of the value of EPI done or value of securities sold.

sources.label: 1787224027885 · Subject: Acceptance of digitally signed Power of Attorney from FPIs · p. 2
sources.text:
This eliminates the need for notarisation, apostillisation or consularisation of Power of Attorney, thereby reducing the overall time taken for FPI onboarding and improving ease of doing business for FPI applicants.

Accordingly, Para 9 (B)(iv) of Part B of the FPI Master Circular stands modified as follows:

SEBI, over the years, has taken various measures to streamline and digitalise the FPI registration process including introduction of Common Application Form (CAF) for the purpose of registration, PAN, bank and demat accounts, permitting the use of Indian digital signatures for executing CAF and other registration documents, facilitating seamless digital signature functionality within the CAF portal and grant of registration based on scanned copies.

sources.label: 1792079571420 · 4.2. Timings of CAS: · p. 3
sources.text:
Trading in index derivatives contracts shall continue until 3:45 p.m. on all trading days, except on expiry days when trading in expiring index derivatives contracts shall cease at 3:30 p.m.

Trading in stock derivatives contracts shall continue until 3:45 p.m. on all trading days, including on expiry days.

The post close session in the cash segment shall operate between 3:50 p.m. to 4:00 p.m., where trades shall be executed at the closing price of securities.

The closing price of securities, for which CAS is applicable, on any special trading session of the Stock Exchanges shall also be determined based on CAS. The duration of CAS in such special trading session shall be equal to the duration of CAS as specified in para 4.2.1 above. The derivative segment on such special trading days shall be closed after 5 minutes from the end of CAS. A 10 minutes post close session on such special trading days shall begin 5 minutes after the close of the derivatives segment.
